why: This is the best line (p0001) and the most direct route to a high score.
purpose: What single-bump shape maximizes R, and does local search on the height vector from a smooth seed beat 2/3?
plan: Run a general randomized height-improver seeded with a Gaussian; if it gains, keep deepening (larger N, finer search, flat-top seeds); if it stalls, switch to parametric tuning.

why: Cheaply tests whether flat-topped f*f can beat the Gaussian.
purpose: In the exp-power family f=exp(-|2x-1|^p), which p maximizes R — is the Gaussian (p=2) optimal or do flat-top (p>2) profiles help?
plan: Grid p, refine around the best, return the best profile; if p>2 wins open a flat-top thread.

why: Keeps a second, off-best-line source of candidate extremal shapes.
purpose: Do other compact bumps (sin^s, (x(1-x))^α, smoothed box) exceed or match the Gaussian's R?
plan: Score each family across its parameter, report best R and shape; feed the best into future deepens.

why: Core question answered; the open question is now the structural lever (asymmetry/flat top), moved to new threads.
outcome: Yes: general height optimization from a smooth seed beats 2/3 decisively, reaching 0.8034 (p0006).

why: Flat-top beat the Gaussian (0.7437) and may combine with asymmetry.
plan: Develop the flat-top line: take p0005's flat-top profile, upsample, and run direct asymmetric height optimization; if it gains feed back to the best line, if it stalls park the flat-top family.

why: Other parametric bump families (0.7355) are dominated by direct height optimization; lower priority.
Top programs are all asymmetric; this tests the mechanism directly.
purpose: Does deliberately lowering ||f*f||_inf via an asymmetric f (peak suppression) raise R beyond 0.8078?
plan: Apply monotone tilts exp(λ(2x-1)) to the p0004 shape over a λ grid, reoptimize briefly, and plot R vs measured peak; if lower peak correlates with higher R, push asymmetry harder; if not, asymmetry is exhausted.

why: p0004's coordinate ascent is inefficient; a real optimizer may find better optima.
purpose: Does a proper gradient-based optimizer (L-BFGS-B with numerical gradient) beat the crude coordinate/perturbation ascent on the best line?
plan: Run scipy L-BFGS-B on the height vector from multistarts on the p0004 shape; if it beats 0.8078 keep deepening with higher N, else fall back to structural changes.

why: The gain was too small to justify further gradient work.
outcome: L-BFGS-B gave only +0.0008 over the crude ascent (0.808554), so a proper gradient optimizer is not a major lever.

why: p0012's tilt sweep is the best line and has not yet been refined at higher resolution or with targeted peak suppression.
plan: Push p0012 with two distinct mechanisms: mass-preserving multi-resolution refinement at N=1000/2000/4000, and targeted suppression of the f*f peak by local dips; if either gains, continue that mechanism, otherwise shift to the symmetric/multi-scale alternative.

why: p0011's near-symmetric 0.829953 makes this a direct challenge to B2.
purpose: Is asymmetry actually necessary for R above 0.83, or can a symmetrized version of p0012 retain most of its score?
plan: Symmetrize p0012 by averaging with its mirror, optimize under a mirror-symmetry constraint, and compare R and ||f*f||inf; if symmetric R stays near 0.8338, asymmetry is not essential; if it drops, B2 is supported.

why: The flat-top line is far below the best but has not yet been combined with the successful tilt mechanism.
plan: Apply p0012-style monotone tilt and block reoptimization to the p0013 flat-top shape; if it reaches above 0.80, keep the flat-top line alive; if not, park it as noncompetitive.

why: The question is answered and a symmetric line is now worth its own thread.
outcome: Asymmetry is not necessary: symmetrizing p0012 and optimizing under mirror symmetry retained R=0.833835.

why: p0019 shows symmetry is viable and halves the search space.
purpose: Can a symmetric-constrained optimizer push the symmetric shape above the current best 0.837273?
plan: Take p0019/p0018, symmetrize, optimize only half the heights under mirror symmetry at N=1000-2000 with multi-scale block ascent restarts and dip suppression; if it reaches ≥0.837 keep the symmetric line, else park it.

why: Both mechanisms gained independently and should compose.
plan: Combine the two winning mechanisms on p0018: dip suppression at the f*f peak followed by multi-scale block-ascent restarts; in parallel run a random structural-perturbation search (smooth bumps added/subtracted at random locations). If either gains, push that mechanism; else shift to higher resolution.

why: Keep the off-best line alive with the now-proven mechanisms.
plan: Apply p0018-style multi-scale restarts plus dip suppression to the p0013 flat-top shape; if it reaches ≥0.80 keep the flat-top line, else park it.

why: p0025 is the new best 0.838635; continue combined dip suppression + multi-scale restarts on p0025, then add random structural perturbations if it plateaus.
plan: Deepen p0025 with combined peak-dip suppression and multi-scale block-ascent restarts; if a restart fails to gain, run random smooth structural perturbations. Stop after 3 experiments without a real gain.

why: The flat-top exp-power line is still far below the best; give it one final p0018-style multi-scale test before parking.
plan: Apply p0025-style multi-scale restarts and dip suppression to the p0013 flat-top shape; if it does not reach 0.80, park A2.

why: Symmetric search reached 0.833835 but has not yet used the combined winning mechanisms.
plan: Symmetrize p0025/p0018, optimize half-heights at N=1000-2000 with multi-scale block ascent and dip suppression; if it reaches >=0.837 keep the symmetric line, else park.

purpose: Can a compact-support or piecewise-linear nonnegative f with controlled tails exceed 0.838635, testing the tail-limit conjecture?
plan: Construct tent/trapezoid/compact-support profiles with adjustable shoulder and support; optimize heights under fixed support and compare R. If it beats 0.838635, branch from it; otherwise record evidence for the tail limit.

why: p0025, p0022 and p0024 each exploited one of these levers; they have not been combined.
plan: Fuse all winning mechanisms on p0025: strong dip scan (widths 0.02-0.24, amplitudes 0.01-0.12, more refine attempts), then progressive upsampling to N=2000,4000,8000,13000 with block ascent (blocks 8-16) at each level, keeping the global best; if it gains, push N higher and add finer dip widths.

why: p0024's strong dip scan paid; narrow multi-width dips at fine resolution are an untested setting of this mechanism.
purpose: Can fine block sizes (2-6) plus multi-width/narrow dips at high resolution flatten the top of f*f further than coarse dips?
plan: From p0024, resample to N=4000, run block ascent with blocks 2-6 and decaying additive/multiplicative steps, then scan narrow dips (widths 0.01-0.06) at the f*f peak, then resample to N=8000 and polish; if it gains, keep this fine-dip line and push resolution.

why: Symmetric-constrained optimizer (p0020) stayed at 0.833835 with full budget, failing its own >=0.837 keep test; symmetric line is not competitive.
Tests the tail-limit conjecture with a genuinely different construction class.
plan: Explore slot: build compact-support piecewise-linear profiles from scratch (trapezoid with plateau [a,b] and ramp width w, plus optional shoulder), scan parameters, then block-ascent optimize; if any beats 0.838635, branch from it, otherwise record evidence for the tail limit.
